nodes.name: ZnO template preparation
nodes.procedure: Uniform distributed ZnO arrays on nickel foam (ZnO/NF) are conducted as the substrate for electrodeposition of NiMo precursor. The prepared ZnO arrays with average lengths about 5-6 μm are uniformly distributed on the skeleton of NF.
nodes.source_text: Firstly, uniform distributed ZnO arrays on nickel foam (ZnO/NF) are conducted as the substrate... The prepared ZnO arrays with average lengths about 5-6 μm are uniformly distributed on the skeleton of NF (Figures S1 and S2, Supporting Information).

nodes.name: NiMo electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Electrodeposition of NiMo precursor (NiMo pre@ZnO/NF) conducted at 60 mA cm^-2 for 3600 s on ZnO/NF substrate.

unit_operations.procedure_snippet: electrodeposition of NiMo precursor conducted at 60 mA cm^-2

nodes.source_text: After the electrodeposition of NiMo precursor conducted at 60 mA cm^-2... depositing time of 3600 s are the optimal conditions.

nodes.name: KOH soaking template removal
nodes.procedure: After identifying the optimal electrodepositing parameters, NiMo pre@ZnO/NF was immersed in 5 M KOH to remove the ZnO templates. The templates cannot be totally removed in 1 M KOH.

unit_operations.name: Immersion
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: immersed in 5 m KOH to remove the ZnO templates

nodes.source_text: NiMo pre@ZnO/NF was immersed in 5 m KOH to remove the ZnO templates (The templates cannot be totally removed in 1 m KOH from Figure S12 in the Supporting Information).

nodes.description: Alkaline HER performance in 1 M KOH (three-electrode)
nodes.source_text: LSV curves of different electrocatalysts are displayed in Figure 3a... tested at 1 m KOH with scanning rate of 5 mV s−1. Ni(OH)2–NiMoOx/NF catalyst displays the most superior HER performance... exhibiting nearly zero onset overpotential (overpotential to attain 1 mA cm−2). To deliver current densities of 10, 50, 100 mA cm−2, corresponding overpotentials are separately 36, 101, and 134 mV... To deliver current densities of 10 and 200 mA cm−2 for alkaline HER, this catalyst requires overpotentials of 36 and 176 mV... The Tafel slope of Ni(OH)2–NiMoOx/NF is only 38 mV dec−1... Ni(OH)2–NiMoOx/NF reveals a Cdl of 168.6 mF cm−2

Inserted image in Figure 3d reveals the multicurrent stability test... The stabilized overpotential is ≈36 mV at the initial step of 10 mA cm−2... When finally altering the current density back to 10 mA cm−2, a steady overpotential of ≈49 mV (increased by about 13 mV) can be observed
The polarization curve of Ni(OH)2–NiMoOx/NF after 2000 CV cycles can still overlap the initial one (Figure 3d)

an electrolyzer was assembled by using Ni(OH)2–NiMoOx/NF both as the cathode and anode to implement urea-assisted water electrolysis... with the assistance of 0.5 M urea, demanding simply 1.42 and 1.59 V to achieve current density of 10 and 50 mA cm−2, respectively (Figure 3f). The inserted image displays the catalyst's well maintaining activity even after 40 h continuous electrolysis at 50 mA cm−2
To drive pure water electrolysis at 10 mA cm−2, required voltage is 1.65 V

The contrastive performance of Ni(OH)2–NiMoOx/NF for OER and UOR are exhibited in Figure 3e... To attain the current density of 50 mA cm−2, a greatly lowered potential of 143 mV is manifested for UOR compared with pure OER... a potential of 0.4 V is merely required to afford 200 mA cm−2

nodes.characterization_summary: Homogeneous rod-like array morphology with smooth surface and macropores ranging from 200 to 300 nm after soaking.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The homogeneous rod-like array still remains after the process of removing the templates, the surface of sample becomes smooth and plenty of macropores ranging from 200 to 300 nm appear from Figure 1d,e.

nodes.characterization_summary: Rod-like structure of precursor confirmed; catalyst after soaking shows mixed crystalline/amorphous character with lattice fringes of 0.268 nm and 0.231 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The precursor's rod-like, rough morphology and amorphous character can be confirmed by Figure 1c and its inserted electron diffraction pattern.

properties.description: High-resolution image showing nanostructure with fibrous or nanowire morphology
High-magnification inset showing atomic lattice fringes or nanoparticle detail

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice fringes with spacing of 0.268 nm and 0.231 nm observed; area marked by red line remains amorphous, confirming mixed-crystal character.
nodes.evidence_snippet: While it is interesting to emphasize that the amorphous sample after soaking partially converts to crystalline phase, which can be proved by emerged lattice fringes with spacing of 0.268 and 0.231 nm in the high-resolution image of Figure 1f.

nodes.characterization_summary: Even distribution of Ni, Mo, and O elements; Ni:Mo atomic ratio around 13:1 confirmed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Conducted EDS technique in transmission electron microscope (TEM) image of Figure 1j corroborates the even distribution of Ni, Mo, and O elements along the matrix.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni:Mo atomic ratio identified as around 13:1, consistent with EDS results.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic ratio of Ni:Mo is identified to be around 13:1 combining the energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS) element contents with inductively coupled plasma (ICP) results.

nodes.characterization_summary: Intense characteristic peaks at 33.04°, 38.54°, 52.10° ascribed to Ni(OH)2 (100), (101), (102) planes; precursor shows no characteristic peaks except broad peak at 44.7° for Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As for the sample after soaking, intense characteristic peaks emerging at 33.04°, 38.54°, 52.10° can be ascribed to Ni(OH)2 (JCPDS 14–117), assigning to crystal planes of (100), (101), and (102), respectively.

properties.description: XRD spectrum of sample after 5M KOH soaking, matches Ni(OH)₂ JCPDS 14-117

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p peaks at 856.8 eV (2p3/2) and 874.7 eV (2p1/3) with 17.9 eV separation characteristic of Ni(OH)2; O 1s at 532.1 eV (Ni(OH)2 hydroxide) and 531.6 eV (Mo-O); Mo 3d at 227.8 eV (Mo4+ in MoO2) and 223.6 eV (Mo6+ surface oxidation).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The spectrum of Ni 2p of crystalline Ni(OH)2 can be divided into four peaks. The major two peaks emerging at 856.8, 874.7 eV with high intensity are indexed to the Ni 2p3/2 and Ni 2p1/3, respectively. The energy separation of ≈17.9 eV coincides with Ni(OH)2 phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: O-H bending vibration peak at 1637.14 cm−1 shifts to 1633.67 cm−1 during HER, indicating weakening of O-H bonds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: When just soaking the electrocatalyst in 1 M KOH for 5 min, the bending vibration peak of O−H bonds emerges at 1637.14 cm−1. As HER proceeds, the peak reveals a red-shift trend from 1637.14 generally to 1633.67 cm−1.
